title: Suriya Reveals Why He Stopped Watching Father Sivakumar's Films Early in Career
excerpt: Ahead of the release of family drama Vishwanath And Sons, Tamil star Suriya opens up about a remark in his early twenties that triggered him to distance himself from his father's acting style.
body:
• Suriya says a minister's remark in his early twenties about copying his father's acting style prompted him to stop watching Sivakumar's films
  • The actor says the decision was about forging his own identity, not rejecting his father's legacy
  • His upcoming film Vishwanath And Sons, releasing August 14, marks a return to family drama after a string of action-driven roles

Tamil superstar Suriya has revealed that a casual remark made when he was around 22 years old fundamentally changed how he approached his acting career. In a candid interview ahead of the release of Vishwanath And Sons, the actor said a comment comparing him to his father, veteran actor Sivakumar, triggered him to deliberately stop watching his father's films.

The Incident That Changed Everything

Suriya recalled accompanying a friend to a minister's house to deliver a wedding invitation. When introduced as Sivakumar's son, the minister studied him and made a prediction that stung. "He looked at me and said, 'Oh, you look like him. You're going to do what he did. You're going to act, and the same thing is going to happen again. You'll copy him, have the same body language, modulation and looks. It's going to repeat for another generation,'" Suriya told Cinema Express.

The comment cut deep for a young man who had entered the film industry almost by accident. "I didn't know I would become an actor. Five days before, I didn't even know that I would be standing in front of a camera and acting," Suriya said of his early days.

"That really triggered me. From then on, I actually stopped watching my father's films and paying attention to his modulations because I didn't want to be compared to him or end up doing what he had done."

— Suriya

A Father's Long Shadow

Sivakumar, who debuted with Kaakum Karangal in 1965, appeared as the lead in nearly 200 films over a career spanning decades. He was one of the prominent faces of Tamil cinema before his sons Suriya and Karthi followed him into the industry. The weight of that legacy was something Suriya chose to address head-on by creating deliberate distance from his father's work.

"I wanted to have my own path and make sure there were no similarities," Suriya said. At the same time, he acknowledged the limits of that project. "Of course, I have the same DNA, so certain similarities can naturally happen. But that incident really stayed with me. I started watching his work a little less, simply because I didn't want to be influenced by it."

A New Identity With Vishwanath And Sons

The revelation comes as Suriya prepares to release Vishwanath And Sons, a family drama directed by Venky Atluri that marks a significant departure from his recent action-driven films. Suriya plays Sanjay Vishwanath, a former international pistol-shooting champion navigating age, family responsibilities and an unexpected relationship.

At the film's audio launch in Coimbatore, Suriya spoke with visible enthusiasm about the project. "Different directors have given me different identities. For me, Vishwanath And Sons will be another new identity. And it is Venky who has given me this identity. It has been a very long time since I did such a character," according to IANS.

Director Venky Atluri, known for directing the hit film Lucky Bhaskar, revealed that Suriya's wife, actress Jyotika, played an important role in shaping the film. "One of the important narrations of Vishwanath And Sons was to Jyotika ma'am. She loved the subject and was happy, especially the first half. The feedback I got from Jyotika ma'am was very helpful," Atluri told Behindwoods.

What to Expect

Vishwanath And Sons features Mamitha Baiju as the female lead, with Radhika Sarathkumar and Raveena Tandon in key roles. The music is by National Award winner GV Prakash Kumar, with cinematography by Nimish Ravi. The film's Tamil Nadu theatrical rights have reportedly been sold on a minimum guarantee basis for Rs 45 crore, making it one of the biggest distribution deals for a Suriya film in recent years.

The film is set for a worldwide theatrical release on August 14, produced by Suryadevara Naga Vamsi and Sai Soujanya under Sithara Entertainments and Fortune Four Cinemas.
